messages:
jamal: Seeing a big p95/p99 regression on hosted text-generation since ~08:12 UTC. p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~620ms, p99 ~1.2s. Errors are low but tail latency is off. Noticed by support ticket #4523. Paging the oncall group :warning:

oncall-bot: ALERT: metric 'api.response_time_ms' p99 > 900 for 7m on cluster=eu-west-1, service=redwood-runtime. Triggered incident workflow.

alex: thx jamal. quick triage: is this across all models or one variant? can you pull per-model p95/p99 on time range 08:00-08:20?

jamal: pulling now. short dump: model=rw-lg-1: p95 610, p99 1180; model=rw-sm-1 (quantized): p95 220, p99 650. So impact seems concentrated on rw-lg-1.

maria: that suggests either rw-lg-1 serving nodes saturated or kernel/runtime regression. any config rollouts in last hour?

jamal: checked rollout history: no config rollouts to routing. but autoscaler pushed two new pods at 08:10 (k8s HPA), pods look Ready. CPU fine. GPU memory shows higher tail usage.

alex: can you check KV cache hit rates and batching stats? if KV cache misses spike, larger models will stall on KV recompute.

jamal: cache hit rate for rw-lg-1 dropped from 92% -> 54% around 08:11. batching latency metric increased too. attaching quick logs:

```
[08:11:23] runtime: kv_cache_miss model=rw-lg-1 shard=3 key=...
[08:11:24] runtime: batch_wait_time_ms avg=120 p90=450 p99=900
[08:11:25] runtime: kernel_compile event=repeat model=rw-lg-1
```

maria: kernel_compile events are bad — sounds like hot kernel eviction or JIT thrash. Could be an infra change or kernel cache eviction due to memory pressure.

support_ian: customer impact: multiple customers complaining about slow completions; highest priority clients on Dedicated are affected. They want a mitigation ASAP.

sre_lead: action plan (short term): 1) enable emergency routing circuit-breaker to divert a fraction of traffic from rw-lg-1 to fallback model rw-lg-1-quant. 2) throttle ingress to rw-lg-1 with a rate cap to protect nodes. 3) disable any non-essential batch aggregation that increases latency. 4) capture heap/proc stats for nodes. 5) page infra team if kernel cache eviction persists.

alex: I can flip circuit-breaker and update routing policy. Proposed fallback policy (apply via routing API):

```json
{
  "policy": "fallback",
  "selectors": {"model": "rw-lg-1"},
  "fallback_model": "rw-lg-1-quant",
  "traffic_shift": {"rw-lg-1": 0.6, "rw-lg-1-quant": 0.4},
  "conditions": {"p95_ms": 500, "duration_min": 5}
}
```
alex: curl to apply (example):

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROUTE_TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  https://control-plane.internal/v1/routing/policies \n  -d @fallback.json
```

jamal: applying now — will start at 08:18. also adding a temporary rate limit on host routing: 

```bash
# set per-model token bucket to 30rps for rw-lg-1
redwoodctl routing update --model rw-lg-1 --rate 30 --burst 60
```

oncall-bot: NOTE: routing policy created id=fbk-2141598765 by alex at 08:18 UTC.

maria: parallel mitigation: remove batch size growth rule so we keep latency stable (we can re-enable after kernel cache stabilizes). Patch config:

```yaml
service:
  batching:
    enabled: true
    max_batch_size: 8    # temporarily limit
    growth_policy: disabled
```

jamal: telemetry update 08:22: p95 for rw-lg-1 dropped to ~420ms, p99 760ms. Cache hit recovering to 78%. Support reporting fewer client complaints.

support_ian: customer update sent: "we've applied temporary fallback and rate-limits to improve tail latency; engineering is continuing investigation and will follow up."

alex: next steps for root cause: 1) collect full kernel compilation traces from affected nodes; 2) reproduce with synthetic load that increases KV cache churn; 3) check recent infra image builds for runtime/kernel changes; 4) consider increasing kernel cache retention or pinning kernels on hot nodes.

maria: long-term guardrails we should implement: - automated circuit-breaker that triggers when model p95 > SLO_THRESHOLD for N minutes (we should default SLO threshold per model). - per-model token-bucket limits to prevent noisy tenants from destabilizing large-model nodes. - auto-fallback to quantized variants in same region before cross-region fallback. - scoreboard with cooldown windows and automatic rollback of routing changes if p95 doesn't improve in M minutes.

sre_lead: agree. propose SLOs: p95_target=250ms, p99_target=800ms. Guardrail trigger: if p95 > p95_target * 2 for >=5m OR p99 > p99_target * 1.5 for >=5m then engage auto-mitigations.

jamal: I'll open a follow-up ticket with reproducer steps and attach kernel traces. Reproducer outline: 1) start 100 concurrent sessions to rw-lg-1 with realistic prompt lengths (avg tokens=120). 2) toggle KV cache warmup off to simulate misses. 3) bump batch window to 100ms to force batching pressure. 4) measure p95/p99 and kernel events.

alex: once we have reproducer, infra can test increasing kernel cache size and disabling JIT evictions.

maria: deployment notes for future: add a feature flag `routing.auto_fallback` with tuning params: min_shift, max_shift, cool_down_mins. default off but enabled for Dedicated customers.

oncall-bot: RESOLVED: incident auto-signal cleared at 08:34 UTC. p95 steady ~240ms across majority, rw-lg-1 ~260ms.

jamal: closing loop: immediate mitigations (fallback + rate-limit + batch cap) brought tail latency down. next: root cause follow-up, infra action on kernel cache, and implement SLO guardrail automation + playbook documentation. I'll assign follow-ups.

support_ian: thanks team. i'll update affected customers with ETA for root cause and next update in 24h.

sre_lead: action items: jamal -> RCA ticket + reproducer, alex -> implement auto-fallback feature flag + integration tests, maria -> infra check for kernel eviction and suggest runtime changes. I'll own the guardrail design doc.

jamal: noted. tagging this thread for postmortem notes. Thanks everyone :rocket:
